title: Severe hypoxaemia and tachypnoea failing high-flow oxygen
summary: A 59-year-old man with severe bilateral pneumonia in the emergency department has persistent tachypnoea despite high-flow nasal oxygen.
rationale: Severe multifocal pneumonia with high work of breathing (spontRate 34, pmus 13, shunt 0.28) demonstrating rapid failure on HFNC with falling ROX index (< 2.85). Re-tests failure to recognise non-invasive failure and delayed intubation.

retestsMistake.clinicalFocus: Timely recognition of non-invasive respiratory failure using ROX index trajectory to avoid emergency crash intubation

source: Roca O, et al. An index combining respiratory rate and oxygenation. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019;199:1368-76; Kang BJ, et al. Failure of high-flow nasal cannula therapy. Intensive Care Med 2015;41:623-32; teaching-convention

changes.vignette: Male 59, height 175 cm, weight 82 kg. Bilateral consolidation with higher work of breathing.

sex.reason: Male patient with larger thoracic volume

heightCm.reason: Taller frame setting PBW to 71 kg

spontRateBpm.reason: Higher tachypnoeic drive driving ROX index down

shuntFraction.reason: More extensive alveolar filling and V/Q mismatch

patient.presentingStory: Four days of rigors, high fevers, and pleuritic chest tightness. Arrived via ambulance on 15 L/min non-rebreather mask with SpO2 89% and tachypnoea at 34/min. Intravenous ceftriaxone and azithromycin commenced.
patient.history: Active smoker (30 pack-years), chronic hypertension on amlodipine. No prior hospitalisations. Independent accountant. Full resuscitation agreed. Height 175 cm, weight 82 kg.

findings.examine: Markedly tachypnoeic at 34/min, intercostal recession and prominent tracheal tug. Unable to speak more than single words. Extensive bilateral crackles across both mid and lower zones. Warm, bounding pulse, capillary refill 2 s.
findings.cxr: Bilateral multifocal airspace opacities, most prominent in right lower and left mid/lower zones. Costophrenic angles sharp. No pneumothorax.
